title: Drishyam 3 Has Crossed ₹278 Crore Worldwide in 10 Days. Georgekutty Is Now Malayalam Cinema's Biggest Franchise.
excerpt: Mohanlal's third outing as the cunning family man earned ₹90 crore from overseas markets alone — a reminder that the Indian diaspora doesn't just watch Bollywood.
body:
Georgekutty is back, and the numbers are staggering.

Jeethu Joseph's **Drishyam 3**, the concluding chapter of the Malayalam crime thriller franchise that redefined what a regional Indian film could do at the global box office, has crossed **₹278 crore worldwide** within 10 days of its May 21 release. That makes it one of the highest-grossing Malayalam films ever made — and comfortably the biggest installment in the franchise that started with a modest ₹75 crore global haul back in 2013.

The numbers tell a story the industry has been reluctant to acknowledge for years: Malayalam cinema is no longer a niche market. It is a global force, and the diaspora is its rocket fuel.

## The Overseas Story

Of that ₹278 crore global haul, an estimated **₹90 crore or more has come from overseas markets** — the Gulf, North America, the UK, Australia, and Southeast Asia. That's not a footnote. That's nearly a third of the film's entire revenue coming from audiences who don't live in Kerala.

For NRI Malayalis, the Drishyam franchise has become a cultural event. The original film and its 2021 sequel were among the first Malayalam titles to receive wide theatrical releases in cities like Houston, Toronto, London, and Sydney. The Hindi remake starring Ajay Devgn introduced Georgekutty to a pan-Indian audience, but the original Malayalam version has always commanded fierce loyalty among the diaspora.

Screening reports from the opening weekend showed packed houses in the US and UK, with some theatres adding extra shows to meet demand. In the Gulf states — where the Malayali expatriate community is one of the largest in the world — Drishyam 3 opened bigger than several Bollywood tentpoles released in the same quarter.

## What Makes This One Different

The first **Drishyam** was a taut, self-contained thriller about a cable TV operator who outsmarts the police to protect his family. **Drishyam 2** expanded the moral stakes, asking whether a man who has committed a crime — even to protect his daughter — can ever truly be free. **Drishyam 3** goes further still.

Without spoiling the plot, this installment confronts Georgekutty with a question the earlier films only hinted at: **what does years of lying do to the liar?** As Filmfare noted in its review, "It treats its characters seriously and resists reducing them into franchise caricatures." The critical reception has been mixed — some reviewers found the pacing uneven and the runtime excessive at 160 minutes — but audiences have clearly voted with their wallets.

Mohanlal, at 65, delivers what many are calling one of his most restrained performances. The Georgekutty of this film is not the quick-thinking improviser of the original. He is a man worn down by his own secrets, older and heavier in ways that have nothing to do with age.

## A Franchise That Changed the Rules

When Jeethu Joseph made the first Drishyam in 2013, Malayalam cinema rarely traveled beyond Kerala and the Gulf. The film changed that calculus permanently. It was remade in Tamil (Papanasam, with Kamal Haasan), Telugu (Drushyam, with Venkatesh), and Hindi (Drishyam, with Ajay Devgn) — and every single remake was a commercial hit.

The franchise helped establish the template that other regional films — from **Baahubali** to **KGF** to **RRR** — would later follow: make the film in your language, let the story do the talking, and the audience will come.

For the Indian diaspora, this matters. Drishyam 3's overseas performance is a signal that NRI audiences are hungry for stories told in Indian languages beyond Hindi. The Gulf Malayali who watches Georgekutty in a Dubai multiplex and the software engineer catching a Saturday show in New Jersey are part of the same ecosystem — one that Bollywood has historically ignored but can no longer afford to.

## What Comes Next

With ₹278 crore already in, Drishyam 3 is on track to cross ₹300 crore worldwide. Its OTT release — likely on a major streaming platform — will be one of the most anticipated digital premieres of the year, particularly for diaspora viewers who couldn't catch it in theatres.

Jeethu Joseph has indicated that this is the final chapter in Georgekutty's story. Whether that holds remains to be seen — the film's box office performance will certainly invite conversations about a fourth installment. But for now, Drishyam 3 stands as proof that Indian cinema's most compelling stories don't always come with the Bollywood stamp.
nri_angle: Drishyam 3 earned ₹90 crore+ from overseas markets — a third of its total — driven by NRI Malayali communities in the Gulf, US, UK, and Australia. The franchise's global theatrical footprint mirrors the Tamil and Telugu diaspora cinema model that has reshaped Indian box office economics.
